changelog: Add a fallback Order Principle that breaks ties among markers inside the same noun phrase by preferring a cut immediately after the noun head, so the noun and its modifiers stay together — addresses the primary finding (NP-splitting) with a different ordering formulation than the sibling candidate.
findings: The prompt fails to prefer cuts that preserve whole noun phrases, instead splitting inside noun-heavy spans and hurting cohesion when pieces are translated separately.
The prompt allows cuts that split off a clause’s assertion from an immediate negation or negative determiner, producing a fragment that alone asserts the opposite of the whole sentence.

diagnosis.why: The new tie-breaker pushed cuts to the position immediately after noun heads when two markers fall inside the same NP, so the model avoided NP-splitting (helping the top-1 choice) but shifted many mid-ranked cut choices later. That change harmed the short-latency bins (≤3, ≤5, ≤7) — where many cuts are kept — by moving sensible comma/clause cuts into the NP and producing worse segmentations overall, yielding a small but significant negative mean.
diagnosis.lesson: When adding an NP-head tie-breaker, preserve the earlier comma/embedded-clause cut preferences used by short-latency budgets (don’t let the NP-head fallback override mid-ranked/punctuation-based cuts).
